title: The organic chemistry of embalming agents in Pharaonic and Graeco-Roman mummies
venue: Nature 413: 837-841 (White Rose repository record, abstract only)
ask_addressed: What chemical technologies is ancient Egypt (Kemet, Khemet) securely documented to have practised, from analysis of objects and texts: pigments (Egyptian blue, Egyptian green, frit), glass and faience, metallurgy (copper, gold, bronze), mummification materials (natron, resins, oils), cosmetics (galena, lead compounds, kohl), dyes, fermentation, medical recipes? Give dates and the kind of evidence (chemical analysis, texts, workshop remains).
quote: The nature of the organic treatments remains obscure, because the ancient Egyptians left no written record of the process.
summary: Frames mummification chemistry: natron as desiccant, organic preservatives needed, no native written record, only Herodotus and later Greek and Roman authors. Reports GC-MS study of dated mummy tissues, wrappings and resinous materials.
limits: Only the abstract record was opened (full text not available there), so the specific compounds and dates found are not cited here.

title: Complex organic chemical balms of Pharaonic animal mummies
authors: Buckley, S.A., Clark, K.A., Evershed, R.P.
venue: Nature 431: 294-299 (White Rose repository record, abstract only)
ask_addressed: What chemical technologies is ancient Egypt (Kemet, Khemet) securely documented to have practised, from analysis of objects and texts: pigments (Egyptian blue, Egyptian green, frit), glass and faience, metallurgy (copper, gold, bronze), mummification materials (natron, resins, oils), cosmetics (galena, lead compounds, kohl), dyes, fermentation, medical recipes? Give dates and the kind of evidence (chemical analysis, texts, workshop remains).
quote: fats, oils, beeswax, sugar gum, petroleum bitumen, and coniferous, Pistacia and possibly cedar resins
summary: Chemical analysis of Pharaonic cat, hawk and ibis mummies overturns the view that animals were only wrapped or dipped in resin.
limits: Abstract only; sample numbers and dating not read. Animal, not human, mummies.

title: Recipes of Ancient Egyptian kohls more diverse than previously thought
authors: Riesmeier, M., Keute, J., Veall, M.-A., Borschneck, D., Stevenson, A., Garnett, A., Williams, A., Ragan, M., Devièse, T., et al.
ask_addressed: What chemical technologies is ancient Egypt (Kemet, Khemet) securely documented to have practised, from analysis of objects and texts: pigments (Egyptian blue, Egyptian green, frit), glass and faience, metallurgy (copper, gold, bronze), mummification materials (natron, resins, oils), cosmetics (galena, lead compounds, kohl), dyes, fermentation, medical recipes? Give dates and the kind of evidence (chemical analysis, texts, workshop remains).
quote: The presence of laurionite and phosgenite in Ancient Egyptian make-up likely stems from synthetic manufacture
summary: Multi-analytical study of 11 Petrie Museum kohl containers: galena and cerussite present; laurionite found in one and phosgenite in another, read as synthetic (citing Walter et al. 1999, which was not opened). Also finds manganese- and silicon-based and organic ingredients.
limits: Eleven objects only. The synthetic-origin claim is cited from earlier work, not newly proven here. The quote is the authors' inference (likely), not a measurement.

title: Simply red: A Late Bronze Age glass ingot from Amarna
ask_addressed: What chemical technologies is ancient Egypt (Kemet, Khemet) securely documented to have practised, from analysis of objects and texts: pigments (Egyptian blue, Egyptian green, frit), glass and faience, metallurgy (copper, gold, bronze), mummification materials (natron, resins, oils), cosmetics (galena, lead compounds, kohl), dyes, fermentation, medical recipes? Give dates and the kind of evidence (chemical analysis, texts, workshop remains).
quote: It is accepted that cobalt blue glass was manufactured at Amarna using a cobalt alum
summary: Analysis of an ingot from Amarna (Late Bronze Age, 14th c. BCE capital) places manufacture in Egypt and supports primary glass production there; background sets out cobalt-alum blue glass and copper colourants, with red glass at Ramesside Qantir.
limits: One ingot. The cobalt alum source (Kharga or Dakhla) is stated as probable. Date and Amarna origin partly rest on find context. Quote confirmed in the full-text PDF on the repository record (abstract does not contain it).
